title: Flatness under compatible ring and module equivalences
statement: Let R and S be commutative rings, M an R-module and N an S-module. If eR:R ≃ S is a ring equivalence, eM:M ≃ N an additive equivalence, and eM(rm)=eR(r)eM(m) for every r,m, then M is flat over R if and only if N is flat over S, with flatness as in [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map].

proof.text: Restrict scalars on N along eR. The additive equivalence is now linear, so use Mathlib Module.Flat.equiv_iff. RingHom.Flat.of_bijective makes eR and its inverse flat. Module.Flat.trans in both directions transports flatness of N; the inverse identities verify the scalar towers.

theorem semilinearEquiv_iff
    {R S M N : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
    [AddCommGroup M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module R M] [Module S N]
    (eR : R ≃+* S) (eM : M ≃+ N)
    (h : ∀ r m, eM (r • m) = eR r • eM m) : Flat R M ↔ Flat S N
